item.description: The US Department of Commerce has added Megaspeed, the Singapore-based cloud computing firm at the centre of the ongoing Nvidia saga, to its trade blacklist, hours after the chip giant reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO following his abrupt departure 11 days prior. In a filing released on Monday, the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security placed Megaspeed International and six other entities in Southeast Asia – widely regarded as Megaspeed’s affiliates – on its Entity List. item.title: US places Megaspeed on blacklist as Jensen Huang returns to helm of Nvidia

item.description: Nvidia’s board of directors unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer, and board director on November 23, 2026. Following the decision, the company announced that Colette Kress would continue as chief financial officer, Harvey C. Jones would remain board chair, an independent investigation into foreign intelligence efforts would proceed, and a search for a new chief compliance officer would commence. item.description: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO, president and board director with immediate effect, after the company determined following input from US officials that the move would not pose a national security risk. item.description: China will set up a new standard-setting task force for brain-computer interface (BCI) technologies, while a state-backed think tank has urged investors to remain patient as the nascent but increasingly crowded sector develops.
